steps.title: Apply online for your study permit (visitor visa issued with it)
steps.why: Most foreign nationals need a study permit to study at a designated learning institution in Canada, and you should apply before you travel. Because your citizenship requires a visitor visa (temporary resident visa) to enter Canada, IRCC issues that visa together with your study permit approval — you don't apply separately or pay another fee, and the visa is printed in your passport, so you must travel with the same passport you applied with and enter Canada before the visa expires. Processing times vary by country, so apply as early as possible; submitting an incomplete application will cause delays because IRCC can't finalize your study permit until your application is complete. If you're a doctoral (PhD) student, check whether you and accompanying family members qualify for faster processing.
prerequisites: An IRCC secure account (used to pay fees, submit the application and check status)
A scanner or camera to make electronic copies of your documents
A valid credit or debit card
Your local visa office instructions for the country/territory you're applying from
The instruction guide read through, and answers prepared for the online tool that generates your personalized document checklist
Biometrics (fingerprints and photo) as required
Valid passport you will use to travel (your visitor visa will be placed in it)
steps.cost: CAN $150 study permit fee; no additional fee or separate application for the visitor visa issued with your approval
steps.time_estimate: Processing times vary by country — apply well before you plan to travel

steps.title: Book and give your biometrics within 30 days of the instruction letter
steps.why: IRCC collects biometrics (fingerprints and photo) for most study permit applications to confirm your identity and help assess your application. After you apply, IRCC sends a biometrics instruction letter and you have 30 days to give them — book your appointment as soon as you can to avoid processing delays. Biometrics are valid for 10 years, making repeat trips to Canada easier.
prerequisites: Study permit application submitted online to IRCC
Biometrics fee paid at the time you submitted your application
Biometrics instruction letter received from IRCC
steps.cost: CAN$85 per individual applicant; maximum CAN$170 total for families applying at the same time (spouse/common-law partner and dependent children)
steps.time_estimate: Book immediately; must be completed within 30 days of receiving the biometrics instruction letter

steps.title: Arrange your international tuition payment before the Term 1 fee deadline
steps.why: Your assessed tuition and student fees appear under "Finances" in Workday once they've been assessed, and Term 1 Winter Session fees are due September 9, 2026 (the first instalment covers Term 1 courses, the first half of two-term courses, and most student fees). Since you're sending funds from outside Canada, start the transfer early enough that the money clears into your UBC account by the deadline — bank wires and transfer services from a major currency corridor are usually quick, but processing days still count. Until your exact fees are posted, use UBC's cost estimator to budget the amount you need to move.
prerequisites: Accepted your offer of admission and paid the acceptance deposit ($3,000 for students on a study permit) through the Applicant Service Centre
Registered for courses so your fees can be assessed
Workday access to view your assessed fees under "Finances"
Standard proof-of-funds documentation prepared for your study permit application
steps.cost: Tuition and student fees as assessed in Workday (use the UBC cost estimator for a pre-assessment estimate); plus any sending-bank wire or transfer-service fees and exchange-rate costs
steps.time_estimate: About 1 hour to set up the transfer, plus a few business days for funds to arrive — initiate at least 1–2 weeks before the September 9, 2026 deadline

steps.title: Prepare your port of entry documents and clear Canadian immigration
steps.why: Your study permit approval isn't your permit — you receive the actual study permit from a border services officer at the port of entry. The officer verifies you meet basic entry requirements, so you must have your passport, port of entry letter of introduction (it contains the permit reference number used to issue your permit), and your eTA or visitor visa ready in hand, not in checked luggage.
prerequisites: Study permit application approved
Port of entry letter of introduction received in your online account
eTA or visitor visa (temporary resident visa) issued, if you need one
Travel booked using the same passport you used to apply for your study permit
steps.time_estimate: 30–60 minutes to organize documents; allow extra time at the border on arrival

steps.title: Apply for your Social Insurance Number (SIN)
steps.why: A SIN is a 9-digit number issued by Service Canada that you need to start working in Canada, file taxes, and access government programs. UBC also requires your SIN for tax purposes, so TA/RA payroll can't be set up without it. Online applications may take up to 5 business days, mail up to 20 business days, and in-person appointments issue the SIN during your visit — applying early avoids payroll delays. Apply online at the Service Canada SIN page; you can also apply by mail or request an in-person appointment if you face barriers applying online. Afterward, add your SIN in Workday. Note that as an international student your SIN will start with "9", indicating temporary resident status, and having a SIN alone is not enough to work — you must also be eligible to work in Canada. Protect your SIN as sensitive personal information and beware of fraudulent calls or emails requesting it.
prerequisites: Arrive in Canada and obtain your study permit at the airport or border crossing (international students can only apply after arrival)

A study permit showing at least one work condition: "May accept employment on or off campus if meeting eligibility criteria, per paragraph R186(f), (v) or (w)...", "May work 24 hours per week off campus or full time during regular breaks...", or "May accept employment on the campus of the institution at which registered in full-time studies"
A copy of your passport (plus a translation if any document is not in English or French)
steps.time_estimate: Up to 5 business days online; up to 20 business days by mail; issued same day if applying in person

steps.title: Enrol in BC's Medical Services Plan (MSP) and buy private coverage for the 3-month wait
steps.why: All people residing in B.C. must enrol in the Medical Services Plan (MSP) to access provincial health benefits like doctor visits, and UBC notes you are required by BC law to register for MSP if you do not have other medical coverage. If you are new to Canada, apply as soon as you arrive: coverage may start three months after your arrival date in B.C. (the balance of the month residence is established, plus two months). Because of that wait period, you should get private health care insurance to cover the gap. Note: if you leave B.C. within 6 months of enrolling, you may have to repay your medical expenses. (The sources provided do not identify which UBC office handles MSP enrolment for graduate students — confirm this with UBC directly.)
prerequisites: Arrived in British Columbia and established residence
ID meeting MSP's ID requirements (see the Apply for MSP page)
Private health insurance arranged to cover the 3-month wait period (or coverage kept from a former provincial plan if moving from another province)
steps.cost: MSP premiums: $0 for Canadian citizens and permanent residents; $75/month for students on a study permit. Private interim coverage is an additional, separate cost.
steps.time_estimate: Apply as soon as you arrive; applying online is the easiest and fastest option. Coverage typically begins about three months after your arrival date (e.g., an August arrival is usually covered from November).

steps.title: Check your MSP application status and plan for the 3-month wait period
steps.why: All people residing in B.C. must enrol in the Medical Services Plan (MSP) to access provincial health benefits like doctor visits. New residents complete a wait period equal to the balance of the month in which residence is established plus two months — so if you're new to Canada, coverage may start about three months after your arrival date in B.C. Confirming your application is progressing and knowing your exact coverage start date tells you how long you must rely on other insurance. The Province advises getting private health care insurance while you wait (or, if you moved from another province, arranging coverage with your former provincial medical plan during the wait period). Note also that coverage depends on residency: if you leave B.C. within 6 months of enrolling, you may have to repay your medical expenses. Completing enrolment is also how you receive your Personal Health Number (PHN) and B.C. Services Card.
prerequisites: An MSP Application for Enrolment already submitted online, in person or by mail
Your arrival date in British Columbia, to calculate your wait period (balance of arrival month + 2 months)
Your application reference/confirmation details and the ID you used to apply
If your coverage will be under an employer, union or pension group plan, your group administrator's contact information
steps.cost: No fee to apply for or follow up on MSP enrolment; budget separately for private health insurance during the wait period
steps.time_estimate: 15–30 minutes to check status and calculate your coverage start date
